name: Metropolis Healthcare Ltd
title: Metropolis Healthcare Ltd - 542650 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Metropolis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 450 crore with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 25.2%, driven mostly by volume.
summary.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY to INR 450 crore, ahead of guidance, with 10% patient volume and 11% test volume growth and no price increase in 18 months. EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR 113 crore (25.2% margin, +210 bps) and PAT rose 26% to INR 57 crore (12.6% margin, +90 bps). Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 14-15% and a 100-150 bps EBITDA margin improvement, with a 27-28% margin target over the next two years. Network expansion continued (300 centers added in Q1, 500+ planned), while the company pruned about 300 low-productivity centers.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY; patient volume ~+13.5%. Specialty within B2C +21%; rural centers +36%.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue +15% YoY (now including Core in the base); patient volume ~+6%. Focus on hospitals, MD labs and institutions, mostly Specialty tests.

segments.name: TruHealth
segments.commentary: 18% of Q1 revenue, +22% YoY; radiology-integrated wellness packages +40%+, premium packages +50%+. Ticket size ~INR 2,500.

segments.name: Specialty Diagnostics
segments.commentary: 40% of Q1 revenue, +17% YoY; target to lift share to 45% from 40%. Genomics portfolio doubled over the past year.

segments.name: Core Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Margin in high single digits (~8% at Q4 FY26 end); target ~25% EBITDA margin within 3-4 years of acquisition. Effective acquisition multiple ~10x FY27 EBITDA per management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Management said business grew healthily in revenue and EBITDA; market leader in 2 of 5 countries. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 14-15%, expected to be primarily volume-led; medium-term CAGR also 14-15% (about 9-10% from patient volume, rest from mix).
EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps in FY27 (the CFO-level answer cited 120-150 bps in one reply); target EBITDA margin of 27-28% over this year and next.
Plan to open ~400-500 centers in Tier-2/Tier-3 towns this year; net addition of 500+ centers in FY27.
Center-to-lab ratio to improve from 1:24 in Q1 to ~1:30 by year-end.
No price increase planned near term; intent to pass on part of inflation at an appropriate time.
FY27 capex expected similar to FY26's INR 65 crore (group basis, including acquired entities).
capex_capacity: FY26 group capex was INR 65 crore; FY27 capex guided to be in a similar range.
Added ~300 service centers in Q1 FY27 and more than 500 over the last 12 months; now operating across 750 towns.
Center-to-lab ratio improved from 1:21 a year ago to 1:24 in Q1; target ~1:30 by year-end.
Lab expansion has been halted for about five quarters; no further expansion beyond 750 towns planned.
Pruned ~300 low-productivity or quality-issue centers this quarter (done after ~2 years), with no material revenue impact per management.
Lab-on-lease model run for ~10 years; number of such labs not disclosed (to be followed up).
demand_pricing: No price increase since January 2025; Q1 growth was predominantly volume and mix, with realisations contributing the balance of the 17%.
Specialty and TruHealth mix drove ~5-6% realisation benefit, per management.
CGHS price revision was the only industry-wide price increase; contribution to Metropolis is about 1% of revenue.
Management described competition as normal; new entrants chasing volume at high servicing costs were said to struggle to make money.
Management said Tier-2/Tier-3 economics are not worse than metros; no GLP-1-specific volume split disclosed.
Q1 seasonality was stronger than usual; management could not fully explain the volume strength and cited possible overflow from Q4 and industry tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Split of patient volume growth between B2B and B2C, and colour on strong Q1 volume despite seasonally weak quarter and delayed monsoon.
qa_highlights.answer: B2C patient volume grew about 13.5% and B2B about 6%. Management attributed Q1 strength to market-access execution and seasonal momentum, but could not fully dissect it; possible overflow from Q4 was one theory.

qa_highlights.question: Does Metropolis run O&M or regional lab management with standalone labs, with profit-share arrangements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already runs a lab-on-lease model for about 10 years, taking over pathologist-run labs fully. Number of such labs was not given; to be followed up.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TruHealth Mind and Body initiative a blend of genomics and advanced radiology, and what growth is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: TruHealth combines blood tests with vitals, basic radiology (X-ray, ECG, sonography) and cognitive/mental health checks. Genomics is not part of it yet. No package-level targets were set.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business is CGHS and did it benefit Metropolis from the CGHS price revision?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS is about 1% of revenue, so the one-time price revision benefit is small. Management expects CGHS empanelment to keep growing, though the one-time benefit will not recur next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance of 14-15% growth conservative, and is Q1 a one-off versus the base-rate growth of peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% for the year, citing a track record of delivering that range over the last two quarters. It declined to focus on quarter-by-quarter seasonality, noting weather-driven unpredictability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 group capex was INR 65 crore and FY27 is expected to be in a similar range, including acquired entities.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 27-28% margin target be split between cost pressures and productivity gains, given Tier-2/3 expansion and raw-material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not expand beyond 750 towns and has halted lab expansion for about five quarters, so new towns and labs should not add margin stress. It relies on operating leverage and productivity gains. Tier-2/3 economics were said to be no worse than metros.

risks_watch: Q1 volume strength (10% patient, 11% test growth) was seasonally unusual and management could not fully explain it; watch whether Q2 volumes hold near 10%, or whether Q1 included overflow from Q4.

Pricing: no price increase since January 2025 and none planned near term; the 5-6% realisation benefit came from mix (TruHealth, Specialty). Watch for any price action as inflation and raw-material pressure build.

Margin path: the 100-150 bps FY27 expansion and 27-28% target depend on the lab transformation program and Core margin rising from about 8% toward 25% over 3-4 years. The CFO-level answer cited 120-150 bps, so the guided range is not fully consistent.
Network: about 300 low-productivity centers were pruned, and more than 500 net additions are planned. Watch the center-to-lab ratio move from 1:24 toward 1:30 and any further rationalisation.
Disclosure gaps: number of lab-on-lease labs, International figures and GLP-1 volume split were not disclosed, and management promised follow-ups.
key_quotes: We exceeded our stated guidance with revenue growing by approximately 17% year -on-year, driven largely by volume growth, while margins expanded through operating leverage and continued efficiency gains.

Usually, Quarter 1 is not a strong quarter for Metropolis. However, this year we saw the revenue sequentially increase by approximately 6%, reflecting seasonal momentum, healthy operating leverage, and disciplined execution.
I will have to come back to you on that, the exact number, because it's spread across the markets and this has been in operation for almost about 10 -odd years now.
In the near future, we are not contemplating a price increase at this stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume-led growth, margins and the 14-15% guidance, which management reiterated. It was cautious on the sustainability of Q1 seasonality and declined to forecast quarter-by-quarter, and evasive on the lab-on-lease count, GLP-1 impact and International figures.
